title: JSON can encode a supplementary-plane character as a surrogate pair
summary: A JSON \u escape takes four hexadecimal digits. A supplementary-plane character can be written as a UTF-16 surrogate pair.
applies: Unicode text and JSON byte records
detail: For example, U+1D11E can be expressed as two consecutive escapes, high surrogate D834 and low surrogate DD1E. The number of parsed code points is different from the number of escape segments.
boundary: The surrogates alone do not form a legal Unicode scalar, and implementations may handle such input differently.
relevance: Compare the original JSON file length to the decoded visible string length.
